title: Integer indexed higher adic graded modules and their canonical operations
statement: Let $B$ be a commutative ring, $I$ an ideal and $V$ a $B$-module. Set $P_q(V)=I^{\max(q,0)}V$ for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, using powers of ideals [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and for $a\geq1$ define $G_a(V)=\bigoplus_{q\in\mathbf Z} P_q(V)/P_{q+a}(V)$, using quotient modules [def-weil-pbc-quotient-module] and direct sums [def-weil-pbc-direct-sum-modules]. The homogeneous class of $x\in P_q(V)$ is denoted $[x]_q$; the total class function is defined to be zero on $x\notin P_q(V)$. The scalar action $G_a(B)\times G_a(V)\to G_a(V)$ is obtained by distributing $[b]_s[x]_q=[bx]_{s+q}$ over finite homogeneous sums. For a submodule $U\subseteq B$, which is an ideal, the multiplication on $G_a(B/U)$ is similarly $[x]_s[y]_q=[xy]_{s+q}$ using multiplication in the quotient ring, and its unit is $[1]_0$. These operations can be constructed by choosing representatives in the defining quotient types; the results are independent of the choices. The definition is also given at $a=0$, when every piece is zero.
